_about: Rules are data. Each carries where the requirement comes from, what the reference implementation calls it, and what the user should DO about it.

_obligations.schema: the freely published VDI XSD says so, mechanically checkable
_obligations.table: a freely published table says so (IDTA 02004 Table 1)
_obligations.container: container mechanics we can check without reading the guideline

_oracle.note: A weak oracle: measured defects exist in it. refKeys use module:key because 13 displayed codes are ambiguous.

rules.title: The file is not a readable ZIP archive
rules.remedy: A VDI 2770 container is a ZIP archive. Rebuild it with a standard ZIP tool and check the file was not truncated in transfer.

rules.title: The archive is empty
rules.remedy: Add the metadata file and the documents. An empty archive cannot be classified as either container kind.

rules.title: The archive is neither a document container nor a documentation container
rules.remedy: Put VDI2770_Metadata.xml at the root of a document container, or VDI2770_Main.xml at the root of a documentation container. Both names are case-sensitive and must not sit inside a folder.

rules.title: A member name would escape the extraction directory
rules.whyOurs: The reference implementation extracts to a temporary directory. We never extract, so we can refuse hostile names outright instead of inheriting the risk.
rules.remedy: Rebuild the archive with plain relative names. Absolute paths, parent-directory segments and backslash separators are not acceptable in a container that will be unpacked by the recipient.

rules.title: The archive exceeds this tool's limits for untrusted input
rules.whyOurs: Supplier archives arrive from outside. A validator must not be a way to exhaust the machine that runs it.
rules.remedy: Split the delivery into several containers, or report the archive to whoever produced it if the size looks unintentional.

rules.title: Containers are nested more deeply than expected
rules.whyOurs: VDI 2770 nests one level: document containers inside a documentation container. Anything deeper is unusual enough to flag rather than silently walk.
rules.remedy: Flatten the delivery so document containers sit directly inside the documentation container.

rules.title: The documentation container has no VDI2770_Main.pdf
rules.remedy: Add the main document as VDI2770_Main.pdf at the root of the documentation container, next to VDI2770_Main.xml.

rules.title: The documentation container holds no document containers
rules.remedy: Add the document containers this handover is supposed to deliver. A documentation container with only a main document delivers no documents.

rules.title: The archive contains folder entries
rules.remedy: Store the members flat, at the root of the archive. Metadata refers to files by name, so a file inside a folder is not the file the metadata names.

rules.title: The metadata file is not well-formed XML
rules.remedy: Open the file in an XML editor and fix the reported position. Nothing else can be checked until the file parses.

rules.title: The metadata file does not conform to the published VDI 2770 schema
rules.remedy: Correct the element or value at the reported line so it matches the schema VDI publishes for VDI 2770. The schema is bundled with this tool.

rules.title: The metadata file tries to expand an entity
rules.whyOurs: A metadata file is data. Entity expansion lets it read local files or reach a host, which no handover document has any reason to do.
rules.remedy: Remove the DOCTYPE and entity declarations. Write the values directly.

rules.title: A file named in the metadata is not in the container
rules.remedy: Add the missing file to the container, or remove its DigitalFile entry from the metadata. The two must agree.

rules.title: A file in the container is not named in the metadata
rules.remedy: Declare the file as a DigitalFile in the metadata, or remove it from the container. An undeclared file is invisible to the recipient's system.

rules.title: The declared file format disagrees with the file name
rules.remedy: Make FileFormat and the file extension agree — application/pdf with .pdf, application/zip with .zip.

rules.title: The document carries no VDI 2770 classification
rules.remedy: Add a DocumentClassification whose ClassificationSystem is VDI2770:2018 and whose ClassId is one of the twelve published classes.

rules.title: The class id is not one of the published VDI 2770 classes
The German class name does not belong to this class id
rules.remedy: Use the German name published for this class id, or correct the class id if the name is the one you meant.

rules.title: The English class name matches neither published rendering
rules.whyOurs: The two freely published sources give different English names for five of the twelve classes, so an English name alone cannot decide conformance. We report which renderings exist and never fail a document on this basis.
rules.remedy: Either published spelling is defensible until the disagreement is resolved. Prefer the IDTA 02004 spelling if the container is destined for an Asset Administration Shell.

rules.title: The language code is not an ISO 639 code
rules.remedy: Write the language as a two-letter ISO 639-1 code, or a three-letter ISO 639-2 code where no two-letter code exists. Regional forms such as de-DE do not belong here.

rules.title: The document version declares no PDF file
rules.remedy: Add the document as a PDF and declare it with FileFormat application/pdf. Other formats may accompany it but cannot replace it.

rules.title: The main document is not released
rules.remedy: Set the main document's LifeCycleStatus to Released before handing the container over. A main document under review is not a delivery.

rules.title: A file declared as PDF is not a PDF
rules.remedy: Replace the file with a real PDF, or correct the declared FileFormat.

rules.title: The PDF is encrypted
rules.remedy: Remove the encryption or the password. A document the recipient cannot open has not been handed over.

rules.title: The PDF makes no PDF/A claim
rules.remedy: Produce the file as PDF/A and make sure the exporter writes the pdfaid identification into the XMP metadata. A PDF that never claimed PDF/A certainly is not one.

rules.title: The PDF claims a PDF/A level; this tool did not verify the claim
rules.whyOurs: Verifying PDF/A conformance needs a full PDF/A validator. Reporting a claim as a verdict would be a lie, so we report it as a claim and say so every time.
rules.remedy: Run a PDF/A validator such as veraPDF if you need the claim verified. This tool only confirms that a claim is present and well-formed.
